🐞 Bugs (2) ---
🟠 **Medium**
1. Reconnections can revert to the old layout 🐞 Bug
>
>Description >
> >
>onAllConnected calls reshard for each completed channel whose reported shard count differs from
>the pool's current count, even if an earlier channel in the same batch already established a new
>layout. When an older-layout connection completes alongside a new-layout connection, processing it
>later rebuilds the pool back to the old layout and closes channels just admitted from the new one.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[core/src/main/java/com/datastax/oss/driver/internal/core/pool/ChannelPool.java[R684-685]](https://github.com/scylladb/java-driver/pull/1462/files#diff-c53eb91e8d709a5a7f6da605b79aeaeabe00bf6da66999c78a1011d9f1b13c28R684-R685) > >```diff >+ if (getShardsCount(channel.getShardingInfo()) != channels.length) { >+ reshard(channel.getShardingInfo()); >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A reconnect batch can contain channels from both sides of a node restart. Processing each differing shard count as a fresh reshard lets a late old-layout result undo the new layout and close newly admitted channels. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- core/src/main/java/com/datastax/oss/driver/internal/core/pool/ChannelPool.java[644-700] >- core/src/main/java/com/datastax/oss/driver/internal/core/pool/ChannelPool.java[410-428] > >## Recommended Fix >Choose a consistent target layout for each completed reconnect batch. Close results that conflict with the accepted layout rather than repeatedly rebuilding the pool for them, and arrange a retry to fill any remaining channels. Add a test with mixed old- and new-layout results in the same batch. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

2. Requests briefly lose shard affinity 🐞 Bug
>
>Description >
> >
>next snapshots shardingInfo and channels separately, while reshard publishes the replacement
>values in separate writes. A request concurrent with the rebuild can calculate its routing-key shard
>using one layout and select a channel from the other, including through the new random fallback when
>that shard exceeds the array length.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[core/src/main/java/com/datastax/oss/driver/internal/core/pool/ChannelPool.java[R182-184]](https://github.com/scylladb/java-driver/pull/1462/files#diff-c53eb91e8d709a5a7f6da605b79aeaeabe00bf6da66999c78a1011d9f1b13c28R182-R184) > >```diff >+ // Both fields are replaced if the node's shard count changes, so read each of them only once >+ ShardingInfo shardingInfo = singleThreaded.shardingInfo; >+ ChannelSet[] channels = this.channels; >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A concurrent request can observe sharding information and channel sets from different generations, causing routing-key selection to lose shard affinity during a rebuild. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- core/src/main/java/com/datastax/oss/driver/internal/core/pool/ChannelPool.java[179-213] >- core/src/main/java/com/datastax/oss/driver/internal/core/pool/ChannelPool.java[391-420] > >## Recommended Fix >Publish the sharding information and its corresponding channel array together as one immutable, volatile routing-layout snapshot. Have `next` read that snapshot once and use both values from it; retain a safe fallback for a genuinely invalid shard suggestion. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
